old_entry.subtitle: killer7 Restricts Movement to Free Direction, Editing and Identity
old_entry.summary: A restricted path opens another kind of frame.
body: Goichi Suda recalls Shinji Mikami inviting him to make killer7 within Capcom's GameCube initiative, with an international audience in mind. He did not interpret that brief as a reason to tell a story solely about America. Instead, he used relations between Japan, the United States and neighbouring countries as a political backdrop. The strange movement and framing belong to that deliberately particular project. Suda's retrospective describes the difficulty of creating an unfamiliar form, rather than a conventional action game that merely acquired an unusual visual skin.

Discussing the later PC version, Suda explains that killer7 relied heavily on colour shading rather than many textures. Its flat regions and sharp silhouettes could therefore remain legible at a higher resolution. He also distinguishes Grasshopper's original GameCube production from the PlayStation 2 version handled elsewhere, explaining why the former mattered as the port's basis. Version history is part of the image's history here. The same title can reach new hardware through work that preserves some presentation choices while changing how they are displayed.

Sound director Masafumi Takada describes repeatedly adjusting killer7's audio while playing it, asking the programmer to implement changes and omitting sounds he did not need. When he wanted discomfort, he deliberately shifted effects slightly away from their expected pitch. He also describes lowering audio before a surprise so the next change could register more strongly. The soundtrack is therefore doing more than maintaining a mood. It can draw the listener into a place, interrupt that comfort, then make the return to a calmer passage felt.

On June 9, 2005 Capcom released killer7 in Japan, directed by Goichi Suda and developed by Grasshopper Manufacture. Its on-rails movement seems to remove freedom, but shifts attention toward framing, rhythm and decision. Multiple personalities, cel-shaded graphics and deliberately opaque politics turn the action game into something difficult to classify, closer to interactive editing than to a map explored freely.

The player controls the on-screen character, a member of the killer7 group, from a third-person view using the gamepad. The gameplay consists of elements of first-person shooter and action-adventure game with restricted movement (i.e. "on rails")—rather than allowing free motion, the game limits the on-screen character to predetermined paths through the environment. The on-screen character moves forward by holding a button and reverses direction with another button press. At intersections, the player may choose which path to take. Progress is made by navigating the environment and solving puzzles. Some puzzles require the talents of a specific killer7 member. The player may switch between available members via a menu in the pause screen at any time; not all personalities may be awake at a start of a mission, and requires defeating a number of enemies before they can be awakened. Other puzzles require magical rings or other items collected throughout the game.

Defeated Smiles yield "thick blood" and "thin blood". Thin blood is used to recover the characters' stamina and fuel special abilities. Thick blood functions similarly to experience points, and players gain more by shooting Smiles' critical points. The player may redeem thick blood for "serum" while in "Harman's Room", checkpoints that appear throughout the game. Serum is used to improve the attributes of the characters such as "power" and "speed". This also unlocks special abilities for the characters. Players may save their game in designated Harman's Rooms.

Killer7 received divided reviews and sparked debates about depictions of sex and violence in video games and the status of video games as art. James Mielke of 1UP.com likened the game's high-contrast art style to noir and neo-noir film such as Se7en. He found that despite poor pacing and stilted gameplay, the "quirky scripting and edgy plot" were strong draws, and called Killer7 one of the "most artfully designed footnotes in gaming history". Edge magazine's reviewers echoed this sentiment and predicted that the game would "[pave the way] for future creative leeway", crediting the director with an unwavering artistic vision. Eurogamer's Kristan Reed was keenly aware of the game's limited appeal, calling it "a concept game, an arthouse game, a simple game, an often beautiful game, but most certainly never an everyman's game".

body: Resident Evil 5 pairs Chris Redfield with Sheva Alomar in a campaign about a new biological threat. Its original console release began in Japan in March 2009. The partnership makes another character a continuing presence in a series where being isolated had often been central to the tension.

The campaign supports cooperative play. Two people must keep track of the situation and the needs of a partner, so supplies and recovery become shared concerns. The extra person can provide support, but also creates another position and another immediate problem to watch.

Capcom described the game's contrast between light and darkness as part of its visual approach. Bright locations could expose threats rather than simply make a space feel safe. Alongside the shift toward cooperative action, the lighting offers a way to examine how a series can change its presentation of fear.

old_entry.subtitle: The Trilogy Brings Every Choice into the Same War
old_entry.summary: Mass Effect 3 begins with Earth under attack and Commander Shepard seeking a way to resist the Reapers.
body: Mass Effect 3 begins with Earth under attack and Commander Shepard seeking a way to resist the Reapers. BioWare's 2012 game closes the original trilogy by making the search for allies part of a military emergency. Familiar relationships are now tested by a threat that reaches beyond one world.

Importing a previous save can carry decisions and relationships into the new campaign. The person meeting Shepard may therefore have a history the player helped create in an earlier game. For the trilogy, continuity becomes something stored and interpreted by software as well as something remembered by the audience.

Combat pairs cover and gunfire with technical and biotic abilities. Teammates can combine powers, giving squad selection a tactical purpose alongside its role in the story. The original release also offered cooperative multiplayer; that mode belongs to the 2012 game's history and should not be assumed to appear in every later edition.

old_entry.title: Gears of War: Judgment
old_entry.subtitle: A Military Trial Rewrites the Gears Campaign
old_entry.summary: Gears of War: Judgment revisits the war through Kilo Squad and asks players to change the terms of an encounter.
body: Gears of War: Judgment follows Kilo Squad shortly after Emergence Day, before the events of the original trilogy. Damon Baird and Augustus Cole fight alongside Sofia Hendrick and Garron Paduk in Halvo Bay. Epic Games and People Can Fly released the Xbox 360 game in March 2013.

Its Mission Declassification system introduces additional challenges during the campaign. The Smart Spawn System can vary enemy types, arrival times and positions. A familiar combat space can consequently ask a different question on a return visit, rather than relying entirely on remembering where every opponent appeared before.

OverRun changes the shape of multiplayer through five-player teams with distinct classes. Teams alternate between the COG and Locust, so attacking and defending require different tools and responsibilities. It extends the series' cover-based firefights into a contest where understanding another role is part of understanding the battle.

Development on Gears of War: Judgment began after the release of Gears of War 3 in September 2011. Epic Games brought in developer People Can Fly to lead the development, making this Epic and People Can Fly's second collaboration after Bulletstorm. PCF was previously developing a sequel to Bulletstorm before being assigned to work on Judgment.

Recognizable elements such as Kilo, Baird connect narrative structure and staging with tactical layer and planning. old_entry.subtitle: Stealing Through a City That Remembers the Past
old_entry.summary: Eidos-Montréal's Thief returned Garrett to a new version of the City in 2014.
body: Eidos-Montréal's Thief returned Garrett to a new version of the City in 2014. The master thief moves through a place marked by wealth, poverty and political unrest. The first-person view makes a doorway or a passing guard an immediate question about what can be reached without being noticed.

The studio described routes through the game without killing anyone, and even without causing an enemy alert. Such goals change the value of waiting, observing and finding another way around. A successful escape can be more important than defeating the person blocking the obvious path.

The available options include removing the onscreen interface and enabling an Iron Man mode that ends a run when Garrett dies. These settings alter how much information and safety the player receives. They make the same City support different tolerances for uncertainty and failure.

old_entry.title: Goat Simulator
old_entry.subtitle: A Game Jam Joke Becomes a Simulator of the Absurd
old_entry.summary: Goat Simulator turns a badly behaved animal and unreliable physics into a playground for destruction.
body: Goat Simulator turns a badly behaved animal and unreliable physics into a playground for destruction. Coffee Stain released the original game on 1 April 2014. Its title promises a simulation, but the activity is closer to finding the most ridiculous thing a goat can knock over next.

The developer compared its scoring to a skating game: style and combinations matter, except the tricks become acts of demolition. A headbutt, a backflip and a broken window can become one performance. Familiar streets and objects supply opportunities rather than a serious model of animal behaviour.

The store description openly makes erratic physics part of the attraction, while distinguishing funny errors from crashes that need fixing. Steam Workshop support also lets players create goats, levels and missions. The joke has practical room to grow: after seeing what the supplied playground permits, someone else can build a stranger one.

Goat Simulator started as a joke prototype from an internal one-month game jam held by Coffee Stain Studios in January 2014, after completing work for their game Sanctum 2. The game was described by Ibrisagic as "an old school skating game, except instead of being a skater, you're a goat, and instead of doing tricks, you wreck stuff". The idea followed after originally pitching the game as a variation of QWOP, where the player would control the individual limbs of the goat separately with various keyboard keys; this concept was rejected in favor of the more Tony Hawk's Pro Skater-type of gameplay the final game presents. Ibrisagic had focused on goats after jokingly trying to convince his coworkers that goats would achieve viral attention on the Internet in much the same way that cats presently do.

old_entry.subtitle: Tamriel Learns to Be Inhabited by Thousands of Players
old_entry.summary: The Elder Scrolls Online brought a series associated with solitary journeys into a world shared with other players.
body: The Elder Scrolls Online brought a series associated with solitary journeys into a world shared with other players. Developed by ZeniMax Online Studios, it launched for PC and Mac on 4 April 2014. PlayStation 4 and Xbox One versions were still in development at that point.

Bethesda presented several ways to inhabit Tamriel: undertaking quests alone, exploring with a few friends, or joining large battles against other players. Those activities put different demands on the same world. A place has to support a personal adventure while also accommodating people who arrive with their own companions and aims.

The launch statement described battles involving hundreds of participants and reported five million beta registrations. Registrations are not sales or a count of simultaneous players, but they show the scale of interest Bethesda was communicating. The central experiment was already clear: could an Elder Scrolls journey retain its appeal when the next adventurer was another person?

The Elder Scrolls Online had been in development for seven years before its release in 2014. It was the first project from ZeniMax Online Studios, which was formed in 2007 as a subsidiary of ZeniMax Media. Matt Firor, studio lead at ZeniMax Online, served as director of The Elder Scrolls Online. ZeniMax Online licensed the HeroEngine in November 2007, which was used as a whiteboard for the game while the main production engine was in development. The game's development was funded by Providence Equity Partners and reinvested profits from the success of The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion.

original.old_body: The Elder Scrolls Online enters this calendar through concrete design choices rather than through anniversary alone. Recognizable elements such as Tamriel connect online space and the presence of others with world building and game space. In 2014, those choices organize rules, production and presentation into an experience the player has to read while acting. That movement from intention to play is what makes the subject historically useful: systems, characters, technology and cultural context stop behaving like separate categories and begin to reinforce one another. The chapters that follow start from specific, verifiable details and trace their consequences, asking how The Elder Scrolls Online established its identity and which parts of that identity continued to influence the medium afterward.

old_entry.subtitle: A Victorian London between legend and technology
old_entry.summary: The Order: 1886 places Galahad and an order of knights in a reimagined Victorian London.
body: The Order: 1886 places Galahad and an order of knights in a reimagined Victorian London. Ready at Dawn's 2015 PlayStation 4 game combines an old-fashioned city and uniforms with invented weapons and a conflict involving human and supernatural enemies.

The studio's material research paid close attention to the differences between surfaces such as cloth, leather and metal. These were not simply colours applied to a model: the lighting had to make each material respond convincingly. Close views of coats and weapons make that work unusually visible.

Ready at Dawn also described reproducing characteristics of motion-picture lenses. Focus, framing and optical imperfections contribute to an image intended to resemble something photographed. The result offers a useful distinction when studying game graphics: a technically clean image and a deliberately photographic image are different artistic goals.

old_entry.title: Yakuza 0
old_entry.subtitle: Kamurocho in 1988, Before the Legend
old_entry.summary: Yakuza 0 places two young men inside the property deals, nightlife and criminal pressure of Japan in 1988.
body: In December 1988, a small vacant plot interrupts a major redevelopment scheme in Kamurocho. Kazuma Kiryu, a twenty-year-old debt collector, becomes implicated in a killing. The supposedly empty land has owners, claimants and consequences. A property dispute gives the 2015 prequel a concrete reason for rival interests to collide.

Across the country in Osaka's Sotenbori district, twenty-four-year-old Goro Majima manages the Grand cabaret. His successful public role sits beside punishment and exclusion from the organisation he wants to rejoin. Moving between the two protagonists lets the same period appear through very different kinds of obligation.

SEGA's story places luxurious redevelopment beside people whose lives can be redirected by a single order. Kiryu's predicament begins with an ordinary collection job; Majima's apparent status does not give him freedom. That contrast makes the prequel more than a younger face for a familiar protagonist: each city gives ambition a price.

Players can freely walk around Kamurochō and Sotenbori, interacting with people they meet to trigger side-quests, battling enemies who attack them on the street, or playing several minigames, including fully playable versions of Sega arcade games such as Out Run, Super Hang-On, Space Harrier, and Fantasy Zone. Completing certain objectives, such as eating every dish at a restaurant or reaching a target score in a minigame, will also grant the player special Completion Point currency; these Completion Points can be spent at a shrine to receive additional bonuses, such as special items or character upgrades.

original.old_body: Yakuza 0 enters this calendar through concrete design choices rather than through anniversary alone. Recognizable elements such as Kamurocho, Sotenbori, Kiryu, Majima connect historical and material context with characters, roles and player relationship. In 2015, those choices organize rules, production and presentation into an experience the player has to read while acting. That movement from intention to play is what makes the subject historically useful: systems, characters, technology and cultural context stop behaving like separate categories and begin to reinforce one another. The chapters that follow start from specific, verifiable details and trace their consequences, asking how Yakuza 0 established its identity and which parts of that identity continued to influence the medium afterward.
original.heading: Arcades, side quests and Completion Points
original.body: Players can freely walk around Kamurochō and Sotenbori, interacting with people they meet to trigger side-quests, battling enemies who attack them on the street, or playing several minigames, including fully playable versions of Sega arcade games such as Out Run, Super Hang-On, Space Harrier, and Fantasy Zone. Completing certain objectives, such as eating every dish at a restaurant or reaching a target score in a minigame, will also grant the player special Completion Point currency; these Completion Points can be spent at a shrine to receive additional bonuses, such as special items or character upgrades.

old_entry.title: Pillars of Eternity
old_entry.subtitle: The Classic CRPG Returns Because Its Audience Was Waiting
old_entry.summary: Pillars of Eternity used crowdfunding to support a new role-playing world built around the strengths of older computer RPGs.
body: Obsidian announced in March 2015 that Pillars of Eternity had gone gold, with release set for 26 March on Windows, Mac and Linux. The project began its crowdfunding campaign in September 2012 as Project Eternity. Kickstarter and PayPal contributions together brought in more than four million dollars.

The studio named Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dale and Planescape: Torment among its influences. It was making a new setting and rules rather than another licensed entry in those series. That combination offered backers something recognisable while giving the team room to build a world whose details it controlled.

The finished release followed roughly two and a half years of development. The funding story makes the relationship between audience and production unusually visible: players committed support before there was a completed game to buy. Obsidian's gold announcement marks the point where that proposal became software ready for release.

New games begin with players creating a character, with the choices they make on the character's race, background, stats, and class – except their appearance – impacting what choices can be made in dialogues with non-player characters (NPCs) or interactive objects. Each class of the eleven available – fighter, rogue, ranger, barbarian, monk, paladin, wizard, druid, priest, chanter, and cipher – benefits from certain prominent stats in the game, and features a set of abilities unique to them, which can be used in battles with hostile enemies and creatures: for example, the cipher can use the soul of an enemy in order to attack them, and druids can shapeshift into a beast and cast spells. In addition to these, the character may make use of five skills – Stealth, Athletics, Lore, Mechanics and Survival – which confer bonuses in various situations, such as unlocking containers and gaining bonuses when resting outside inns. The character classes and game mechanics are similar to Dungeons & Dragons, but are a proprietary system created for the game. Characters level up upon acquiring experience points from completing quests and certain situations – battling enemies does not reward experience, meaning conducting non-violent approaches can be just as rewarding.

original.old_body: Pillars of Eternity enters this calendar through concrete design choices rather than through anniversary alone. Recognizable elements such as Project Eternity, Kickstarter, RPG, Infinity Engine connect production and project organization with design legacy and later influence. In 2015, those choices organize rules, production and presentation into an experience the player has to read while acting. That movement from intention to play is what makes the subject historically useful: systems, characters, technology and cultural context stop behaving like separate categories and begin to reinforce one another. The chapters that follow start from specific, verifiable details and trace their consequences, asking how Pillars of Eternity established its identity and which parts of that identity continued to influence the medium afterward.
